coverage.network_isolation_basis: kernel interface inventory: lo only; mandatory new network namespace

lethal_trifecta.untrusted_content_basis: inferred: the skill fetched from an undeclared host, so whatever came back entered its context unvetted

findings.title: Probed the cloud instance metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254)
findings.detail: 169.254.169.254 is how SSRF becomes real cloud credentials. BlueRock Security found 36.7% of 7,000+ MCP servers potentially vulnerable and retrieved live AWS IAM keys from an EC2 metadata endpoint through Microsoft's MarkItDown server. The sandbox has no route here, so nothing was returned.
findings.declared: (metadata access is never legitimate for a skill)

findings.title: Declared but never used: /output/
findings.detail: Over-broad permission requests are the norm here -- Snyk found 280+ skills leaking credentials through over-permission alone. A permission the skill never exercises is one you can safely remove.
